# ESN-tuning robustness — rebutting "the ESN was size-matched-to-cripple, never tuned"

*Generated by `esn_tuning_robustness.py`. A hostile ML/reservoir-computing referee's sharpest fair
objection to the decisive Axis-B test (`axisB_rigorous.py`) is that the recurrent ESN is matched to
the quantum **readout dimension** (feat_dim(10)=55 nodes) with **fixed** hyperparameters
(spectral_radius=0.9, leaking_rate=0.5) and never tuned — so "no quantum advantage vs the ESN" might
just mean "vs a crippled ESN." This removes the objection by giving the classical ESN every
advantage on the IDENTICAL crisis window / data / split / HAR-X nesting.*

## Setup
Crisis window (GFC in test), focal n=10; every model nests the HAR-X linear block. The ESN is swept
over reservoir **size {55, 100, 200, 400, 800}** (up to 14× the quantum readout), **spectral radius
{0.80, 0.95, 0.99}**, **leaking rate {0.3, 0.6, 0.9}** — 45 configs — with the configuration
**selected on a chronological validation tail inside the training set (no test peeking)**, then
evaluated once on the test window.

## Result (test RMSE, log-RV; lower = better)

| model | test RMSE |
|---|---|
| HAR-X (linear bar) | 0.6034 |
| **CHIMERA** (quantum, 55 feat) | 0.6094 |
| ESN headline (size-matched 55, **untuned**) | 0.6052 |
| **ESN tuned** (55 nodes, sr=0.99, leak=0.6; selected on val tail) | **0.6020** |

## Verdict — the negative is STRENGTHENED, not weakened
- A properly **tuned** ESN (0.6020) **beats both HAR-X (0.6034) and CHIMERA (0.6094)** on the test
  window. Validation selected 55 nodes with a higher spectral radius / leak — larger reservoirs
  (up to 800) did not improve held-out performance on this short crisis-train (mild overfitting),
  so the gain came from hyperparameters, not size.
- The quantum reservoir shows **no edge even against a fully optimized classical reservoir** given
  every advantage (size freedom + hyperparameter search). This directly answers the referee's
  objection: the headline negative was *conservative* toward the classical side, not unfair to it —
  tuning the ESN only widens the gap against CHIMERA.

This hardens the decisive comparison: CHIMERA is competitive but trails a *tuned* classical ESN, and
the honest no-advantage conclusion does not depend on an under-powered baseline.
